review_type: independent AI review; NOT human expert gold
scope: All 300 unordered pairs of the 25 Math9 questions, using only the permitted corpus. No old research, other agent outputs, external sources, APIs, computed answers or proposed repairs.

judgment_policy.plausible_conditional: Same visible target task and response form, subject to unresolved points/answer and context verification; NOT complete safe substitution.
judgment_policy.reject: Visible target skill, task, output scope or demand differs enough that generic topic overlap or matching solutions do not justify substitution. Not a claim that an educator could never repurpose the item.
judgment_policy.uncertain: Insufficient visible evidence to choose either category; not needed for this corpus under the strict task-equivalence policy.

key_findings: Only A1/B1 and A2/B2 match both the visible target operation and response form; their A-side point allocation and both answer keys remain unverified.
The B header assigns 0.5 points to each question; A1/A2 have no individual point allocations. A3/A4/A5 explicitly show 2.0/2.0/3.0 points.
The first document retains a multiple-choice / 3.0-point heading over subsequent constructed-response questions; no silent section repair or allocation was inferred.
B15 has singular-number wording versus a paired-number option; B16 may conflate sufficient singleton conditions and a complete solution condition. These are flags, not repaired items.
The B15/B16 apparent solution-set match, A4/B7 proportional geometry data, B3/B10 shared radical simplification, and A5/B18 tangent relationship do not establish task-preserving substitution.

limitations: This is independent AI judgment, not human expert gold or a calibrated difficulty study.
Only corpus text/HTML was read. No rendered images, browser layout, curriculum mapping, prior research, source documents, student performance or external keys were inspected.
No answers were invented, calculated into a key, or repaired. Multiple-choice options are not authoritative answers.
Point allocation is distinguished from answer verification: known point equality alone is insufficient; unknown allocations remain unknown.

No item explicitly references another question; local givens/configurations were treated as self-contained, not as shared cross-item dependencies. Absence of a diagram in the supplied HTML was not automatically treated as a defect where textual geometry is sufficient.
Reject decisions are conservative slot-equivalence decisions, not statements that the questions are invalid or unusable in other assessment contexts.
All 300 pair records explicitly compare tasks, forms, points, dependencies, answer availability and visible defect flags; repeated missing-key caveats intentionally remain pair-local.
